root_causes.description: The frontend service exhibits a severe p99 latency spike (~9600-10000ms vs ~24ms p50 baseline) while every downstream dependency (checkout, cart, payment, product-catalog, recommendation, shipping, currency, ad) remains fast (p99 < 25ms). The bimodal distribution (p50=24ms, p99=9600ms) with zero errors, flat CPU/memory, no restarts, no pod events, and normal request rate (~1.8 req/s) indicates latency is introduced within the frontend itself, not propagated from a dependency or caused by resource exhaustion.

evidence.expected_baseline: all downstream services p99 < 25ms, confirming latency originates at frontend, not a dependency

root_causes.description: The latency is concentrated in checkout user journeys (user_checkout_single/user_checkout_multi traces at ~15s), suggesting a latency fault specifically affecting the frontend's checkout-page request path (e.g., an injected delay or misconfigured feature flag/timeout on checkout-related handlers) rather than a uniform slowdown of all frontend endpoints.

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_multi=15022ms, status ok; all top slow traces are checkout journeys (also 5ef152882a37196a=15008ms, 281180d463e9c90b=15010ms), 0 errors
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout journeys complete in < 1s; downstream checkout service p99 is only 24.850ms

evidence.observed_value: p50=24.018ms vs p99=9600.969ms — bimodal distribution indicating only a subset of requests (checkout flows) are slow
evidence.expected_baseline: p50 and p99 within the same order of magnitude (< 100ms)

root_causes.description: flagd shows a small persistent error rate (mean 0.021, max 0.029) during the window; however, this is minor, stable, and uncorrelated with the shape of the frontend latency spike, so it is likely unrelated background noise rather than the root cause.

evidence.observed_value: flagd error_rate mean=0.021, p50=0.019, p95=0.029, max=0.029; frontend error_rate=0.000; all other services 0.000
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; flagd's small stable error rate does not explain the frontend p99 latency anomaly

remediation_steps: Inspect the frontend deployment for recently injected latency faults or chaos experiments (e.g., artificial sleep/delay on checkout handlers) and remove/rollback the change; verify p99 returns to the ~24ms baseline.
Check flagd feature-flag configuration for any latency-inducing flags toggled on the frontend checkout path and disable them.
Review frontend code/config for blocking calls, missing timeouts, or retry storms on the checkout request path, since all downstream services (checkout p99=24.850ms) are healthy.
Add per-endpoint latency SLO alerts on the frontend (p99 > 1s for 2 minutes) to catch bimodal latency regressions earlier.

If a chaos experiment is active, terminate it and confirm recovery by re-querying histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="frontend",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[2m])) by (le)).
